proof:
# Even the weaker continuous Gamma_3 bound fails for a sampled fold
fiber compatibility, transverse erosion, and nonheavy fibers to give a
continuous depth theorem for the folded measure. It is NOT an OC
counterexample. Its folding anchor is an actual interior point of the
neighboring fiber, but is explicitly NOT a globally deepest contact.

## 1. Actual convex body and the mass-preserving sampled fold

Let T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)} and V=|T|=1/2. Put

    A=(7/15)T, K=T, R=T,
    C=conv({-1}xA, {0}xK, {1}xR).

The extreme integer fibers are A and R. The middle section is exactly
K because (A+R)/2=(11/15)T is contained in T. Thus the full-dimensional
body C has exactly these three integer fibers, all of positive area.
Its total mixed area is (499/225)V, and its largest fiber has area
V<(499/450)V=M/2. These are strictly nonheavy actual fibers.

Choose the interior point p=(1/300,1/300) of R. Fold just the fibers
with z<=0 toward the anchor (1,p), using

    Phi(z,x)=(x-zp)/(1-z).

This is a map of the two selected fiber measures to the continuous
plane, not a change of the mixed-integer lattice. At z=0 it is the
identity; at z=-1 it is x -> (x+p)/2. Its area Jacobian on the latter
fiber is1/4. The pushforward measure therefore has Lebesgue density

    f=1_T+4 1_(cT+tau(1,1)),
    c=7/30, tau=1/600,
    integral f=(1+4c^2)V=(274/225)V.                 (1)

All support sets and coefficients are exact. In particular, the
large weight4 is the actual sampled-fiber Jacobian; it is not an
independently assigned density parameter.

## 2. Three rational caps cover the whole plane

Set s=27/50, r=4/15 and k=(1-r)s/2=99/500. Consider

    H0={x+y<=s},
    H1={x-r y>=k},
    H2={y-r x>=k}.                                   (2)

These closed halfspaces cover R^2. Indeed a point outside H1 and H2
has (1-r)(x+y)<2k=(1-r)s, hence belongs to H0. Consequently every
point of the plane lies in a halfspace of (2) whose f-mass is at most
the largest of their three masses. This is a valid upper bound on
the maximal continuous halfspace depth of f; it requires no claim
about where a deepest point occurs.

Divide all masses in the next calculation by V. The cap H0 cuts a
triangle of relative area s^2 from T. It contains the whole smaller
triangle, since c+2tau<s. Thus

    b0=mass_f(H0)/V=s^2+4c^2=11461/22500.             (3)

The H1 cap at vertex(1,0) has relative area(1-k)^2/(1+r).
Translating the inner triangle changes its threshold to
k' = k-(1-r)tau, with 0<k'<c. Its relative cap area is
(c-k')^2/(1+r). Therefore

    b1=mass_f(H1)/V
      =[(1-k)^2+4(c-k+(1-r)tau)^2]/(1+r)
      =6566561/12825000.                             (4)

Coordinate interchange gives mass_f(H2)/V=b1, and direct rational
comparison gives b1>b0. Equations(1)-(4) prove

    max_y depth_f(y)
       <=6566561/15618000
       =27/64-89131/62472000 < Gamma_3=27/64.         (5)

In particular replacing a proposed Gamma_2 bound for this folded
measure by the smaller continuous Gamma_3 bound does not fix it.
The certificate is three actual rational halfspaces and exact areas,
not a numerical optimization or an assertion about experimental
extremizers. All their boundaries are null for the density in(1).

## 3. Scope of the obstruction

The underlying perspective sections satisfy the usual actual convex
Minkowski erosion inclusions, since p is in int R. A transverse section
of R through p has positive length. Thus those geometric inclusions
alone cannot imply the failed continuous-depth bound.

The anchor (1,p) is not a deepest mixed-integer point. At the exposed
endpoint base, an integer tilt can isolate any own cap. The own cap
x+y<=1/150 through p has area V/22500, whereas the centroid of the
middle T already has mixed depth at least Gamma_2 V. Hence this example
does not contradict a hypothetical additional theorem requiring two
genuine deepest contacts. The independently audited critical-contact
example in `candidate fc66a0bec6505bfb`
disproves Ball-body convexity, but does not assert the stronger depth
upper bound(5). These two obstructions have deliberately distinct scopes.
